aces.system.onStart: Runs once when the scene starts.
aces.scene.onEnd: Runs once when the scene ends (changing or restarting scene).
aces.system.everyTick: True every frame (about 60 times per second).
aces.system.compareVar: Compare a global or scene variable with a value.
aces.system.compare: Compare any two expressions, e.g. Player.x > 10.
aces.system.isTrue: True when the expression is true (or not 0).
aces.system.isBetween: True when a value is between min and max (inclusive).
aces.system.chance: True randomly, e.g. 25 = one time in four.
aces.system.once: Put last: the event runs only once each time the other conditions become true.
aces.system.isGroupActive: True if the event group is active.
aces.system.repeat: Runs the actions and sub-events several times. Use loopIndex for the current number.
aces.system.for: Repeats the rest of the event, counting from start to end (both included). Use loopindex("name") for the current number.
aces.system.while: Repeats the rest of the event as long as the conditions after it are true (or until "Stop loop").
aces.time.timerFinished: True at the moment a timer started with "Start timer" runs out.
aces.time.isTimerRunning: True while a timer is counting down.
aces.time.compareTime: Compare the seconds since the scene started.
aces.system.setVar: Change the value of a global or scene variable.
aces.system.addToVar: Increase a variable (text variables get the value appended).
aces.system.restartScene: Start the current scene again from the beginning.
aces.system.wait: Pause the rest of this event (next actions and sub-events) for a while.
aces.system.waitPrevious: Pause the rest of this event until what the actions above it started has finished: a Tween, a Move to position, a play-once animation. Then the next actions run, e.g. slide a panel in, wait, then show its text. Nothing to wait for means no pause. An object destroyed or a tween stopped meanwhile counts as finished.
aces.system.waitUntil: Pause the rest of this event (next actions and sub-events) until the expression is true, e.g. Score >= 10 or Door.y > 5. It is checked every tick. If it is already true the event goes on at once. Careful: in an event that runs every tick, a condition that never comes true keeps adding waits.
aces.system.log: Show a short message on screen.
aces.system.consoleLog: Write a line to the debug console (🐞 button while playing) without showing it in the game. Great for checking that an event runs, e.g. "Clicked! score = " + Score.
aces.system.alert: Pop up a message box and pause until it is closed. Use it for one-off checks, not every tick.
aces.system.callFunction: Run a function block (made with Add → Function) with values for its parameters.
aces.system.setReturnValue: Inside a function: the value that Functions.Name(...) gives back.
aces.system.stopLoop: End the loop this event is in (Repeat, For, For each, While) after the current repeat.
aces.system.setTimeScale: 1 = normal speed, 0.5 = slow motion, 2 = double speed.
aces.system.vibrate: A short buzz you can feel, great with Shake camera. Works on Android phones; ignored on desktop and iPhone.
aces.system.save: Store a value on the device (kept after closing the game). Empty value = the variable with the same name as the key.
aces.system.load: Read a saved value into a variable (nothing happens if it was never saved). Empty variable = same name as the key.
aces.system.setGroupActive: Turn a group of events on or off.
aces.system.create: Create a new object from a prefab (or copy of an object) at a position. It becomes picked for the next actions.
aces.time.startTimer: Start a countdown. Use "On timer finished" to react when it ends.
aces.object.collidesWith: Runs at the moment the object starts touching another object. In its actions, hitX, hitY, hitZ are where they touched, hitNormalX/Y/Z the surface direction (out of the other object toward this one), hitSpeed how fast they met and hitImpulse how hard they were pushed apart.
aces.object.collisionEnded: Runs at the moment two objects stop touching.
aces.object.isTouching: True while the object touches (overlaps) another object. In its actions, hitX, hitY, hitZ, hitNormalX/Y/Z, hitSpeed and hitImpulse describe the current contact (for triggers hitX/Y/Z and the surface direction are estimated and hitImpulse is 0; all 0 when nothing touches).
aces.object.compareVar: Compare one of the object's own variables (e.g. hp).
aces.object.compareProp: Compare position, angle, size or speed, e.g. Player y < -5.
aces.object.isOnGround: True when a physics object is standing on something.
aces.object.isInVehicle: True while the object rides a vehicle (after Enter vehicle).
aces.object.hasDriver: True while someone is in this boat or car (after Enter vehicle).
aces.object.isInWater: True while the object is inside a Water object — for a physics object, while any part of it is.
aces.object.onEnterWater: Runs when a physics object enters a Water object, as soon as any part of it is under the surface.
aces.object.onLeaveWater: Runs when a physics object comes all the way out of a Water object.
aces.object.isEmittingParticles: True while its Particle System is making new particles.
aces.object.isPlayingParticles: True while its Particle System plays: emitting, or particles still flying after a stop. False when paused or finished.
aces.object.isPausedParticles: True while its Particle System is paused ("Pause particles").
aces.object.compareParticleCount: How many of its particles are alive right now.
aces.object.onParticleCollision: Runs when particles of the object hit another object. Needs its Collision module with "Send Collision Messages" on. In its actions, hitX, hitY, hitZ are where the first one hit, hitNormalX/Y/Z the surface direction and hitSpeed its speed after the hit.
aces.object.onParticlesStopped: Runs when its Particle System has stopped and its last particle died. Needs "Stop Action" set to Callback in the Particle System.
aces.object.isPlayingAnimation: True while the given model animation is playing.
aces.object.onHurt: Runs when the object (it needs the Health behavior) takes damage and survives or dies. Its health is in Self.health.
aces.object.onDeath: Runs when the object’s health reaches 0 (it needs the Health behavior). It is still there during this event, then removed unless Destroy on death is off.
aces.object.onArrived: Runs when the object reaches the point of its "Move to position" (or gets as close as it can when walls are in the way).
aces.object.isMovingTo: True while a "Move to position" is under way.
aces.object.onAnimationFinished: Runs when a play-once animation (loop off) reaches its end. Leave the name empty for any animation.
aces.object.hasLineOfSight: True when nothing solid (walls, crates…) is between the object and the target, e.g. an enemy only chases the player it can see. Triggers (checkpoints, coins) never block the view.
aces.object.isMoving: True when the object's physics speed is above zero.
aces.object.isTweening: True while a tween of that property is still running.
aces.object.isVisible: True if the object is shown.
aces.object.hasTag: True if the object has a tag.
aces.object.onTap: Runs when the player taps this object on screen (also works for UI buttons).
aces.object.onCreated: Runs when a new instance of the object is created.
aces.object.onDestroyed: Runs when an instance of the object is destroyed.
aces.object.distanceTo: Compare the distance between the object and the nearest other object.
aces.object.count: Compare how many of this object exist (or are picked).
aces.object.exists: True if at least one of these objects exists. Invert it for "no more coins".
aces.object.pickNearest: Only use the instance closest to another object.
aces.object.pickFarthest: Only use the instance farthest from another object.
aces.object.forEach: Run the actions and sub-events once for every instance, one at a time.
aces.object.destroy: Remove the object from the game.
aces.object.spawn: Create an object (prefab) at this object's position (+ offset). The new object becomes picked for the next actions.
aces.object.setPosition: Teleport the object. Self.x means "keep the current x".
aces.object.move: Move the object by an amount (world axes). Multiply by dt for smooth per-second movement.
aces.object.moveForward: Move in the direction the object is facing.
aces.object.moveToward: Move toward another object (speed in meters per second).
aces.object.moveTowardPosition: Move toward a point (speed in meters per second).
aces.object.moveToPosition: Walk to a point on the ground over the next frames (speed in meters per second), going around walls and rocks when "Go around walls" is on. A model plays its walk clip (sprint above "Sprint above speed") and idle when it stops, unless "Play walk / idle animations" is off. "On arrived" runs when it gets there. Tap to move: X = touchWorldX, Z = touchWorldZ.
aces.object.stopMoving: Cancel a "Move to position" (it stays where it is, without "On arrived").
aces.object.setAngle: Turn the object to face a direction (degrees around the vertical axis).
aces.object.rotate: Turn the object by some degrees. Multiply by dt for smooth per-second rotation.
aces.object.lookAt: Turn the object to face another object.
aces.object.setEnabled: A disabled object is hidden and stops moving/colliding.
aces.object.tween: Smoothly animate position, angle, size or opacity to a value, e.g. size 1.5 with Back for a pop, or Self.y + 2 to rise. Starting another tween of the same property replaces it. On a UI element, x and y are its position on the screen (in canvas pixels, from its anchor), angle its rotation, size its scale and opacity its fade (children follow); z does nothing.
aces.object.stopTweens: Stop every running tween of the object where it is now.
aces.object.attachTo: The object becomes a child of the target and moves with it, e.g. a key the player picked up. It stays where it is; use Set position afterwards to place it relative to the target (0, 0, 0 = the center of the target).
aces.object.enterVehicle: The object (usually the player) gets into a vehicle — an object with the Boat or Car behavior: it sits in the vehicle’s Seat and rides along, its own movement stops and cameras following it follow the vehicle (the vehicle’s Auto seat and Auto camera settings switch these off if you do them yourself). It does not steer the vehicle: pass the input in with Drive car / Move with input. Undo it all with Exit vehicle.
aces.object.exitVehicle: Gets out of the vehicle it is in: it is put down beside it (on land if one side has some) and moves on its own again; the vehicle stops being driven.
aces.object.driveCar: Drives a Car (Driver "manual"): steer −1 (left) … 1 (right), gas 0 … 1, brake 0 … 1. Use it every tick the controls are held (e.g. under "On button Gas held"); when the event stops running the car coasts. Works with your own buttons, a touch wheel or anything else in events.
aces.object.setMoveInput: Moves the object like the joystick does, from events: x −1 (left) … 1 (right), y −1 (back) … 1 (forward). Works for a Platformer, Top-down movement or a Boat. They never read the joystick themselves, so pass it in: x = joystickX, y = joystickY. Use it every tick the input is held (e.g. under "On button Left held"); when it stops, the object stops.
aces.object.simulateControl: Presses one of the movement controls for this tick, like the joystick or a key would: Left / Right steer and strafe, Up is gas / forward, Down is brake / reverse, Jump jumps, Handbrake locks the wheels. Use it every tick the control is held (e.g. under "On button Left held"). Several at once in the same tick stack up, so Left + Up steers and accelerates together. Works on Platformer, Top-down, Car and Boat. They never read the joystick themselves: this and Move with input / Drive car are the only things that move them.
aces.object.detach: Let go of an attached object: it stays where it is and moves on its own again.
aces.object.callScript: Run a function from one of the object's code scripts. In the script, write "export function name(a, b) {…}". Fill only the arguments the function takes. To use its result in a condition or value, write Object.script("Script", "name", a, b) in an expression.
aces.object.setVar: Change one of the object's own variables.
aces.object.addToVar: Increase one of the object's own variables.
aces.object.subtractFromVar: Decrease one of the object's own variables.
aces.object.setVelocity: Set the physics speed on each axis (needs a Rigid body).
aces.object.applyImpulse: Give the object a sudden push (needs a Rigid body).
aces.object.applyForce: Push continuously (use every tick; needs a Rigid body).
aces.object.jump: Jump up, only when standing on the ground (needs a Rigid body).
aces.object.damage: Take health from the object (it needs the Health behavior). "From" is what hit it, e.g. Bullet: with Knockback on, it is pushed away from that.
aces.object.heal: Give the object health back, up to its Max health (it needs the Health behavior).
aces.object.setText: Change the text shown by a text object.
aces.text.setText: Change the text of an object with a Text component, e.g. "Score: " + Score.
aces.text.appendText: Add text at the end of the current text.
aces.object.playAnimation: Play a clip of its 3D model, e.g. "walk", "jump" or "die". Loop off = play once and hold the last frame.
aces.object.burstParticles: Shoot some particles at once, e.g. sparks on a hit or a puff on landing. Needs a Particles component.
aces.object.emitParticles: Shoot particles at once with values of your own instead of those of the Particle System: a velocity (x, y, z in its simulation space: own space for Local, world space for World), size, lifetime or color. Leave a field empty to use that setting of the Particle System; an empty velocity axis counts as 0 once any axis is filled. A position (same space as the velocity) starts them there instead of at the emitter, e.g. at hitX, hitY, hitZ; an empty position axis counts as 0 once any axis is filled.
aces.object.spawnParticlesAt: Play a ready-made effect once where the object is, e.g. Sparkles when a coin is collected (works even if you destroy it right after). No Particles component needed.
aces.object.startParticles: Start its Particles component. Running it while the emitter is already going has no effect, so it can sit under a condition that holds for many ticks; a one-shot effect such as Explosion plays again once the previous one has finished.
aces.object.restartParticles: Play its Particles component from the beginning, even if it is already going (bursts again).
aces.object.stopParticles: Stop making new particles. The ones already flying finish their life, or go at once.
aces.object.pauseParticles: Freeze its particles where they are. "Start particles" carries on from there.
aces.object.clearParticles: Remove every particle it has out right now (it keeps emitting if it was).
aces.object.setParticleStartColor: The color new particles start with (Color over Lifetime still multiplies it).
aces.object.setParticleStart: A start value of new particles: speed (m/s), size (m), lifetime (s), rotation (degrees), gravity modifier, or how fast the whole system runs.
aces.object.setParticleModule: Switch one module of its Particle System on or off while the game runs.
aces.object.setParticleRate: How many particles it makes per second, e.g. a bigger fire or a stronger engine trail.
aces.object.playSound: Play the sound of the object's Audio component.
aces.object.stopSound: Stop the sound of the object's Audio component.
aces.object.setBehaviorEnabled: Turn one of the object's behaviors on or off.
aces.object.setBehaviorParam: Change a behavior setting, e.g. platformer speed.
aces.object.removeTag: Remove a tag from the object.
aces.ui.onClick: Runs when the player taps a UI button (e.g. Start, Pause, Retry).
aces.ui.isPressed: True while the player holds a UI button (e.g. a custom fire button).
aces.ui.compareValue: Compare the value of a slider or bar, e.g. Health value ≤ 0.
aces.ui.onValueChanged: Runs when the player drags a slider to a new value (e.g. a volume setting).
aces.ui.show: Show a UI element or a whole screen (and everything inside it).
aces.ui.hide: Hide a UI element or a whole screen.
aces.ui.toggle: Show it if hidden, hide it if shown.
aces.ui.setText: Change the text of a label or button, e.g. "Lives: " + Lives.
aces.ui.setPosition: Move a UI element on the screen: x (right) and y (up) are its Rect Transform’s anchored position, in canvas pixels from its anchor, the same numbers as in the inspector. Leave a field empty to keep that axis. For a smooth slide use Tween (x / y) instead.
aces.ui.setValue: Set a slider or bar value, e.g. health or time left.
aces.ui.addValue: Add (or subtract with a negative number) to a slider. Stays between its min and max.
aces.ui.setMax: Set the maximum of a slider.
aces.ui.setMin: Set the minimum of a slider (0 by default).
aces.ui.setInteractable: Grey out a button or slider so it takes no input, or turn it back on (Interactable).
aces.ui.setImage: Change the picture of an image, button or panel.
aces.ui.setFont: Change the font of a label or a button's text to a font in Files. Leave it empty for the default font.
aces.ui.setBackground: Change the background color of a button, panel or bar.
aces.ui.setTextColor: Change the text color of a label or button.
aces.ui.setFillColor: Change the fill color of a slider or bar.
aces.input.buttonDown: True while an on-screen button (or key) is held down.
aces.input.buttonPressed: True at the moment a button is pressed.
aces.input.buttonReleased: True at the moment a button is released.
aces.input.onTap: True when the player taps anywhere on the screen.
aces.input.screenTouched: True while a finger is on the screen.
aces.input.onSwipe: True when the player swipes in a direction.
aces.input.joystickMoving: True while the joystick (or WASD / arrows, or a gamepad stick) is pushed.
aces.input.joystickDirection: True while the joystick is pushed in a direction.
aces.input.keyDown: True while a keyboard key or gamepad button (PadA, PadB, PadX, PadY, PadLB, PadRB, PadLT, PadRT, PadStart…) is held.
aces.input.keyPressed: True at the moment a keyboard key or gamepad button (PadA…) is pressed.
aces.input.showButton: Show an on-screen control button (Scene → Controls) hidden with Hide.
aces.input.hideButton: Hide an on-screen control button (Scene → Controls). A hidden button can’t be pressed — not with a finger, keys or a gamepad — so it only works where it makes sense, e.g. only while the player touches the boat.
aces.input.setButtonLabel: Change the text on an on-screen control button, e.g. “Board” next to the boat and “Leave” while sailing.
aces.audio.play: Play a sound from your assets.
aces.audio.stop: Stop a sound (leave empty to stop all sounds).
aces.particles.spawn: Play a ready-made effect once at a position, e.g. an Explosion at Enemy.x, Enemy.y, Enemy.z. No object needed.
aces.debug.drawPoint: Debug: draw a small cross at a position to see where it is, e.g. at Enemy.x, Enemy.y, Enemy.z. Shapes are drawn over the game and are for testing.
aces.debug.drawLine: Debug: draw a line between two positions, e.g. from the Player to the Target, to check distances and directions.
aces.debug.drawSphere: Debug: draw a wire sphere to see a range or radius, e.g. how far an enemy notices you.
aces.debug.drawCircle: Debug: draw a ring lying flat on the ground at a position, e.g. an area or a spawn radius.
aces.debug.drawBox: Debug: draw a wire box around a position to check a size or an area, e.g. a trigger zone.
aces.camera.shake: Shake the screen, great for hits and explosions.
aces.camera.lookAt: Turn the main camera toward an object.

behaviors.platformer: Walk and jump when your events or scripts tell it to (needs a Physics body)
behaviors.topdown: Move in 8 directions when your events or scripts tell it to
behaviors.car: Gas, brake, steer when your events or scripts tell it to (needs a Physics body)
behaviors.boat: Sail on water when your events or scripts tell it to (needs a Physics body)
behaviors.cameraFollow: Put on the camera to follow a target
behaviors.destroyOffscreen: Removes the object when it falls or goes too far
behaviors.draggable: Player can drag it with a finger

components.mesh: Visible 3D shape or model with a material
components.camera: Shows the game world from this object
components.canvas: Where UI elements are drawn: the screen, or a place in the scene
components.collider: Lets the object touch and bump into others
components.text: On-screen text like score or messages
components.ui: Text, button, image, slider or panel
components.water: Lake or sea: things float, characters swim

snippets.joystick: Walk around with the on-screen joystick (or WASD / arrow keys).
snippets.jump: Press the "jump" button to jump. Needs a RigidBody + Collider.
snippets.tapmove: Tap the ground and walk there, around walls.
snippets.spin: Rotate constantly around the up axis.
snippets.follow: Chase the entity named "Player" and stop when close.
snippets.patrol: Walk back and forth between two objects you pick in the Inspector (each enemy its own).
snippets.spawner: Create a "Coin" (prefab or object name) near this entity every second.
snippets.coin: Put on the Player: touching a Coin destroys it and adds 1 to Score.
snippets.tapcolor: Tap the object to cycle through colors.
snippets.fall: Restart the scene if this entity falls below the world.
snippets.scorehud: Global script: keeps a Text entity named "ScoreText" updated.
snippets.swipe: Swipe left/right to switch between 3 lanes, swipe up to jump.
snippets.vehicle: Put on the Player. Press the "use" button next to a boat or car (tag #vehicle) to get in or out. Seating and the camera are automatic; steering is yours.
snippets.drivecar: Put on a Car, Boat or Platformer object. The behavior never reads the joystick: you pass it in.
